questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have been to Japan several times before and loved the culture and the people. I wanted to explore the country even further and try to live in such a different culture. It was crucial to me that it was a country and a city I wanted to live in. I did not mind the school, but wanted to be able to experience living in a different city than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think KU could have been better at gather the people going to Tokyo. I actually only met two others because we went to the same school, but there is plenty of spots and three different schools you can go to in Tokyo, and I feel like KU did not do anything in order for us to meet each other.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Hmm KU has been bad at assisting us. KU is really slow when replying and overall I feel like I was really left alone and had to figure everything out for my self. Though, it was not that hard to figure it put but still I think KU could have been better

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: hmm not super difficlt. There is a lot of "Sharehouses" in Tokyo, so you could search for that. I lived in the one called Dash living Ebisu but there is also something called Borderless house

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: especially when attending Chuo, Chuo is located far out of the city so I did not live with any of my class mates and did not really become friends with them. I met some other people I lived with.
